One of my friends has been bringing his dad along wherever we go. We've been to clubs, and his dad comes along. I've told my friends I don't want them to bring their dads over, but one by one, they come, followed by their dads. Specifically, on one occasion, I introduced this group to my current girlfriend, and she was really creeped out. She said the dad cornered her and forced her to have a conversation about cooking and different dishes for about half an hour. The point is, when I hang out with all my friends in their early 20s, I don't exactly want to hang out with a dude in his late 40s. He's not a bad guy, but he gets drunk like he's one of the boys and engages in locker room talk about women who are our age. I find this really disturbing. I've asked some of the guys who are his sons about it, and weirdly, they think it's cool that he hangs out with them and considers him one of the boys. Apparently, he had his kids really young and was married already in his early 20s and didn't have the opportunity to get drunk and party with his friends. So now he does it with his son and his friends. Next time the group hits me up, I really want to ask if his dad is going to be there. I love my friends and still want to hang out with them, but the dad being around ALL THE TIME is too much. I get if we're drinking at his house and wants to hang out, but going out with us or coming to MY house when I didn't know he was coming is a problem. So, the question is: Is it morally acceptable for me to ask my friend if his dad is going to be there before I agree to hang out with them? Alright, let's think about this. Morally, is it wrong to want to avoid someone who makes you uncomfortable? I mean, if someone's behavior is making me or my girlfriend uncomfortable, isn't it reasonable to want to avoid that situation? On the other hand, the dad is just trying to spend time with his son and his friends. He didn't have the chance to party when he was younger, so now he's doing it. His intentions might be good, but his actions are causing discomfort. Is it wrong to exclude someone based on their behavior? Or is it about setting boundaries to ensure everyone feels comfortable? Also, considering that the dad is engaging in conversations that make my girlfriend uncomfortable, and he's cornering her, that's a form of harassment, right? It's making her feel uneasy, and that's not acceptable. So, by asking if the dad is going to be there, I'm essentially setting a boundary to protect myself and my girlfriend from an uncomfortable situation. That seems reasonable. But then, is it fair to the dad? He's just trying to be part of the group. Maybe I should talk to him directly about how his behavior is making people uncomfortable. But if I'm not comfortable doing that, maybe it's better to just avoid situations where he's present. In the end, I think it's morally acceptable to ask my friend if his dad is going to be there before agreeing to hang out. It's about ensuring that everyone's comfortable and that the environment is respectful.
